name: Alicia Nielsen
life: “I have opened a hotel before sunrise for fourteen winters.” People around the corner by Juniper Tailor know Alicia by a small Wednesday habit. Alicia looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I stood at the old stop for three days. Each day a different person waited with me so I wouldn't look foolish.
appearance: Alicia is easy to recognize by brown hair pinned away from the temples and heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Usually dressed in a washed violet jersey with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges, Alicia folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing when listening.
personality: Alicia can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To make the old stop a useful meeting point during the change.
family: Ellen Soto is Alicia’s cousin. Alicia puts the kettle on. Ellen chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *An empty dedication*, Ellen says, “I am a character in the book by accident. I want the dedication to leave my real name alone.”
connections: Stella Hull. An old-stop regular walks the new wheelchair turn alongside its advocate.

reactions.situation: The route manager declares the move a success
reactions.response: Alicia asks one rider from each corner to walk the new distance.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Alicia asks the driver to come back on foot and look at the damaged goods before discussing cost.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Alicia asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
